bullets.title: August CPI prints hot at 0.29% core m/m — markets price 88-90% odds of September Fed hike
bullets.body: Core CPI came in at 0.29% m/m (vs ~0.20% consensus), the largest monthly reading since April, driven by lodging (+2.36%), airlines (+2.68%), communications services (record jump), and a reversal higher in shelter (0.3% after 0.1% in July). Markets immediately repriced to 88-90% probability of a September FOMC hike; Wolfe expects hikes at both September and December. Core PCE is tracking a softer ~0.22-0.25% m/m, but multiple desks argue the Fed faces a credibility problem if it holds given energy and services stickiness.

bullets.title: Fed rate hike path extending: 3-4 hikes priced through 2027; 10yr yield approaching 5%
bullets.body: 22V Research puts core PCE consensus at ~30bp — well above Fed's 15bp comfort threshold — with nominal GDP running 6.6% y/y and M2 growing 7% annualized over six months. The 10yr Treasury yield is approaching 4.98% (2023 cycle high); 22V's target is 6% and Hedgeye warns that a close above 4.98% opens 5.29%. JPM financials desk sees 3-4 total hikes priced through 2027. Underlying inflation runs 100+ bp above target with marginal rents re-accelerating after a period of softness.

bullets.title: Brent crude near $100/bbl on Mideast/Houthi risks; oil now positively correlated with yields, not cuts
bullets.body: Brent pushed toward $100 (touching $108 intraday per UBS consumer staples note) driven by geopolitical risk from Iran and Houthis, with Red Sea/Gulf export disruptions persisting per AIS vessel data. Critically, 22V and Hedgeye both flag that oil prices now correlate positively with yields rather than signaling rate cuts — a regime shift with implications for 60/40 portfolios. Goldman Sachs is hosting a rapid-response webinar Monday on navigating the oil breakout.

bullets.title: S&P 500 +1.1% to 7,673 post-CPI; market interprets hike as credibility-restoring, not bearish
bullets.body: Despite the hawkish CPI print, S&P 500 futures held +1.08% to ~7,680 with the Nasdaq leading at +1.32%. Desk color suggests the market views a September hike as removing uncertainty and anchoring long-end yields — net positive. Hedge fund positioning is reportedly light with low net exposure, providing a downside cushion. SPX 7,600 is flagged as the key SpotGamma negative-gamma pivot; Hedgeye's immediate-term resistance is 7,670.

bullets.title: Market rotating INTO AI/momentum, OUT OF non-AI cyclicals and rate-sensitive names
bullets.body: 22V and Hedgeye both identify a sharp factor rotation: AI-exposed long-short baskets up 2%+ over the past two weeks while consumer discretionary and non-AI cyclicals lag. High variable-rate debt / non-AI consumer names turned sharply bearish in August. Russell 2000 remains in bearish trade and trend, with high-yield spreads widening to ~266bp and CCC-rated debt yielding ~15%. Energy-adjusted liquidity is deteriorating in a pattern similar to 2022.

bullets.title: ECB hiked; third hike by year-end is base case — BoE likely to shift hawkishly at next meeting
bullets.body: ECB raised rates and gave non-committal guidance; 22V sees a third ECB hike by December as base. JPMorgan previews the BoE holding next week at 3.75% but flagging a hawkish shift — CPI could peak at 4% or higher by early next year, wages tracking 3.5% vs BoE's 3.1% forecast, and GDP tracking 0.9% above post-war expectations. A November BoE hike is the base case; QT pace expected to slow from £70bn to £50bn annually starting October.

bullets.title: UBS: Rising bond yields offset equity growth optimism; yields likely to stabilize, growth continues
bullets.body: UBS strategy argues that rising discount rates have largely offset the surge in equity growth optimism, but expects bond yields to stabilize near current levels, allowing equity growth to continue. This is the counterpoint to the more bearish 22V/Hedgeye views — UBS is not calling for sustained yield dislocation.

bullets.title: MSFT plans to triple data center capacity to 38GW by 2032; AI compute scarcity is real
bullets.body: Microsoft disclosed plans to expand from ~12GW today to 38GW by 2032, adding ~4-4.5GW/year, roughly 2/3 CPU and 1/3 AI GPU. OpenAI has paused new $200/month ChatGPT Pro (Astra) subscriptions due to unprecedented compute constraints. ORCL's Q1 results showed GPU renewal contracts repriced at ~20% premiums, directly validating neocloud pricing power. The AI compute scarcity narrative is now well-supported across ORCL, OpenAI, and hyperscaler capex disclosures.

bullets.title: ORCL Q1 OCI +121% y/y; backlog breadth widening with 24-hour acceptance turnover — FCF inflection 1-2 years out
bullets.body: Oracle's Q1 beat on OCI revenue (+121% y/y constant currency), maintained $90-95B capex guide, and completed the full $20B ATM equity raise. Q2 guidance calls for +30-34% cc growth; FY guide of $90B+ was in line. GPU resales at 20% premiums and 24-hour contract acceptance turnover signal an extremely tight supply/demand environment. FCF inflection is estimated 1-2 years out as capex peaks; 22V pegs CRWV realizations at $15-20M/MW/year vs consensus ~$12M.

bullets.title: USD/JPY technically broken below 155 support; DXY bearish trend despite short-term bounce
bullets.body: JPMorgan FX technicals flag USD/JPY breaking through key May-August range support at 155.04-155.32, threatening a broader retracement of the April 2025-July 2026 rally. Next supports are 151.85, then 150.00-150.88. DXY is bouncing within a holding pattern but remains below 100.08-100.35 resistance with a neutral technical bias. Hedgeye characterizes the USD as in a bearish trend, with dollar weakness supportive of crypto and global liquidity.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi summit September 24: trade, tech controls, Taiwan, capital flows all in scope
bullets.body: Jefferies is hosting a preview call September 14th ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting scheduled for September 24. Key investor watch points include USMCA-parallel tech export controls, Taiwan posturing, supply chain realignment, and capital flow implications — particularly relevant for names with China revenue exposure.

bullets.title: PCE housing inflation at new cycle lows but marginal rents re-accelerating — watch for 2027 CPI reversal
bullets.body: PCE Housing Price index rose only ~18bps in August with 3- and 12-month rates at new cycle lows. However, one analyst notes marginal rent inflation is 'perking up' after a period of softness, and real-world rents picking back up suggest CPI rent/OER could reaccelerate in 2027. The gap between average and marginal rent growth has narrowed dramatically, meaning government measures can now be taken more at face value.

bullets.title: Financials facing near-term de-grossing on rate hike path; asset-sensitive names FITB, EWBC preferred
bullets.body: JPM financials desk warns that 3-4 rate hikes bad for near-term risk appetite in GSIBs, investment banks, and wealth managers, with curve flattening unfavorable for earnings upgrades. Regional bank index KRE shed ~5% as 3M-5Y spread accelerated to 75-80bps. However, underlying loan growth and credit remain positive; banks screen well on capital return. Asset-sensitive names FITB and EWBC are the preferred plays; de-grossing may create buying opportunities in better franchises.

bullets.title: Global REIT sector down 2.9% in August; rising yields the key headwind; US outperforming at +16.7% YTD
bullets.body: Global listed real estate declined 2.9% in August, trimming YTD returns to 9.1%, with the US still the standout at +16.7% vs Europe +0.5% and Asia -3.1%. Rising bond yields from sticky inflation and geopolitical uncertainty are the primary valuation headwind. The 10-year at 4.92% and continuing bond selloff drove the S&P 500 RE Index to underperform the broader market by ~30bps yesterday.

bullets.title: Healthcare premium inflation at 7.1% YoY; employers shifting costs to employees — long-term bearish on provider consumption
bullets.body: PPI for group medical insurance running 7.1% YoY in August 2026, well above the historical 2-5% range, driven partly by federal dollar pullback from the healthcare system. Employers absorbed premium inflation in 2025 but are now passing marginal costs to employees, with the Employment Cost Index trailing PPI by 200bps. Long-term outlook is bearish on provider consumption as cost-shifting, coverage rollbacks, and GLP-1 coverage cuts cascade into deferred and lost downstream procedures.

bullets.title: Consumer staples under pressure: Brent above $100 inverting HPC performance; XLP -5% since late August
bullets.body: UBS consumer staples desk notes Brent at $108 this week is pressuring health & personal care companies' input costs, with oil and HPC performance showing a negative 59% correlation over the past 29 weeks. XLP is down ~5% since late August. KMB guided Q3 materially below expectations (sales down low-single digits vs Street flat, EPS down low-teens vs Street -8%). European HPC names Henkel and Beiersdorf are flagged as most at risk; Haleon best positioned.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples contracting: IGV -0.7% YTD vs S&P +13.6%; All-SaaS index at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index is trading at 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales, down 4.9% week-over-week. All-Security at 8.2x (down 4.5% WoW) and All-Vertical at 5.9x (down 7.5% WoW). IGV is down 0.7% YTD versus S&P 500 up 13.6% — a meaningful underperformance that reflects the rotation away from non-AI software names and monetization uncertainty (ADBE being the poster child).

bullets.title: Political resistance to AI data-center power demand emerging as regulatory risk for buildout timelines
bullets.body: Roth Capital is fielding a 1,000-1,250 person consumer survey in high-density data center regions (PJM, ERCOT) to quantify blame attribution of AI data centers for rising electricity bills and assess whether electricity cost is becoming a voting issue. Ohio has already canceled a $1.5B data-center tax exemption. Separately, Crux AI (Google/Blackstone) is facing delays from unsuitable sites and transformer shortages. This political overlay is an underappreciated risk for power generators and data center operators.

bullets.title: Commodity bull market broadening: Bloomberg Commodity Spot Index at all-time high; potash, phosphate, urea all inflecting higher
bullets.body: The Bloomberg Commodity Spot Index is at an all-time high per 22V, with fear-driven commodity bull markets historically self-sustaining. Mizuho's commodity monitor shows US Midwest potash up $10/st to $403, phosphate up $10/st to $855, and urea up $15/st to $500 on higher energy and crop prices. Corn sits at $5.33/bu on Ukraine/Russia grain disruptions and lower US yield expectations; USDA expected to trim corn yield to 178.1 bu/ac.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 bearish; high-yield stress at ~266bp spreads and CCC debt at ~15% yield signal credit deterioration
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains a bearish trade and trend view on the Russell 2000 (IWM), citing its historically strong correlation with high-yield deterioration. High-yield spreads widened to ~266bp with corporate yields rising ~12bp; CCC-rated debt is yielding ~15%, indicating stress. The Russell 2000 is down 2.6% on the week despite being up 16.5% YTD, underperforming the S&P 500 by 0.6% this week. Telecom and Financials are the top-performing sectors within the index; Health Care, Basic Materials, and Discretionary are the worst.
